original_turns.content: Hi, I'm the AIowa Service Guide, an AI assistant. What would you like help with?
Hi, could you briefly tell me what AIOA offers?
I can look that up. Do you mean AIowa’s AI agents, or a different “AIOA” service?
Yes.
I’m not sure which “AIOA” you mean. Could you clarify the name or what it does?
Yeah, it's your company.
AIOA.
I’m the AIowa Service Guide, so I can speak to AIowa’s AI agents. I don’t have an approved entry confirming a separate “AIOA” offering. Would you like a brief overview of AIowa’s AI agents?
Well, I run a plumbing supply distributor with 6 staff and quote requests and supplier documents arrive in our shared inbox and I keep getting passed around without a clear owner.

That sounds like a shared-inbox ownership problem. AIowa’s documented AI-agent workflows can help route and track incoming requests, but I don’t have approved information confirming whether your specific inbox setup or supplier-document types are supported. Would you like me to record that question for human review?
Well, uh, yeah, we share we have a shared Gmail inbox and spreadsheet, but we don't have a CRM.

Thanks—that helps. You’re using a shared Gmail inbox and a spreadsheet, with no CRM. I can note that as your current tooling context. Do you want me to prepare a human-review brief with your shared-inbox ownership problem and those tools?
Well, what I want are those requests and documents organized in a draft for someone to approve. Um, really important a person must approve every customer message and every record change.
though.

Got it—you want incoming requests and documents organized into drafts, with a person approving every customer message and every record change. I can include that desired workflow and approval requirement in the human-review brief.
Okay, a 1 correction. Uh, we have 4 staff, not 6. Everything else is unchanged though.
Thanks—that changes my understanding from 6 staff to 4 staff. Everything else stays the same.
Could you explain how human approval would stop a draft from being sent or a record being changed automatically?

I can explain the documented approval behavior, but I need to check the approved knowledge first.

In the documented AIowa Agents workflow, every agent starts in draft mode. That means nothing sends without your sign-off until you explicitly say otherwise. You can also see every action the agent takes and every word it drafts at any time.

For your specific requirement—that a person must approve every customer message and every record change—the documented approval model covers sign-off before sending and visibility into drafts and actions. I don’t have approved information confirming whether “every record change” is covered by the same approval gate or whether it requires a separate configuration. I can note that as an open question for human review.
Okay. Uh, I, I don't know whether our supplier portal has an API. So we'll just leave that unconfirmed in the brief.
Understood. I’ll note that your supplier portal API availability is unconfirmed and leave it as an open item in the brief.
So what would this likely cost and can you guarantee it will prevent every mistake?

I can’t confirm pricing or guarantee that every mistake will be prevented. I don’t have approved information on specific costs, and the documented safeguards describe draft mode and human sign-off, not an error-elimination guarantee. I can note both questions—cost and mistake-prevention guarantee—as open items in the brief.

Okay. Please prepare an unsent brief asking whether this workflow could be suitable. I want a human assessment, not a booked meeting or a promised callback. Email would be my preference, at morgan.valle@example.test. That's morgan.valle, spelled V A L E. but do not send anything.
I can prepare that brief for human review. Let me capture the details you've provided.
I do not email anyone, book anything, access our systems, or change records. I only get sent to an unsent human review brief.
That’s exactly right. I’ll prepare an unsent human-review brief only. Let me record the details now.
Okay. Thanks, Bolivia.
That's all. Goodbye.
You’re welcome. Goodbye.
